Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the AetherCloud Technologies Q2 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during the Q&A, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing AetherCloud Technologies's results for the Q2 FY2024. With me on the call are Sarah Kline, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; and Raj Patel, Chief Product Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Kline.

Sarah Kline:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. AetherCloud Technologies had an exceptional Q2, exceeding expectations across all key metrics. This success is a testament to our innovative technology, dedicated team, and strong customer relationships.

During the quarter, we focused on five key areas:
1. Expanding our market share in key verticals.
2. Investing in cutting-edge research and development.
3. Enhancing our cloud security posture.
4. Driving operational efficiencies.
5. Strengthening our ecosystem partnerships.

One of our fastest-growing segments is multi-cloud and hybrid cloud partnerships, which represent a strategic imperative driving significant revenue acceleration. In Q2, this area delivered 28% year-over-year growth to $2.8 billion, with multi- and hybrid-cloud solutions contributing a record $1.1 billion, up 52% YoY—more than double the growth of our core single-cloud infrastructure offerings. This reflects enterprises prioritizing flexibility to address vendor lock-in, data sovereignty, and rising egress fees.

Gartner data shows 68% of enterprises now pursue multi-cloud strategies, up from 55% 18 months ago, while hybrid adoption has reached 74% in regulated sectors like finance and healthcare. We're leading with our Aether MultiCloud Fabric (MCF), an orchestration layer enabling seamless portability across AWS, Azure, GCP, and our AetherCloud Platform. MCF supports over 15,000 Kubernetes clusters worldwide, delivering average TCO reductions of 32% via automated egress optimization and federated identity management using OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect.

Key partnership updates include our expanded Azure alliance, co-engineering the Aether-Azure Hybrid Bridge—a zero-trust extension of Azure Arc for managing VMware vSphere and bare-metal alongside Azure services. This generated $450 million in joint Q2 bookings, including top global banks, with Azure Arc hybrid deployments up 67% quarter-over-quarter and sub-50ms AI inference via Azure OpenAI integrated with Aether Edge Runtimes across 120 locations.

With Google Cloud, our Anthos on Aether integration achieved Anthos Service Mesh certification, supporting GKE migrations to AetherCloud with 99.99% SLA continuity. Anthos revenue grew 240% YoY to $320 million, highlighted by a European automotive OEM moving 40% of SAP S/4HANA workloads to a hybrid setup, cutting deployment from 12 weeks to 72 hours using GitOps with ArgoCD and Flux.

Hybrid shines with VMware and Red Hat post-Broadcom acquisition; we support VCF 5.1 with Tanzu Kubernetes Grid. Our Aether Hybrid Sovereign Suite serves data residency in 14 countries, including new Saudi Arabia and Indonesia clouds. Q2 hybrid revenue hit $330 million, up 49% YoY, including a $150 million U.S. defense contract for air-gapped OpenShift on Aether Bare Metal with Intel SGX and AMD SEV-SNP for FedRAMP High and CMMC 2.0.

North America led at 62% of bookings ($680 million) via AWS co-sell and 1,200 net new logos. EMEA grew 71% YoY to $280 million on GDPR/Schrems II, with a UK NHS Trust migrating 5,000 VMs for 28% savings and HITRUST. APAC rose 55% to $140 million via GCP-Anthos; China pilots with Alibaba yield 40% PoC conversions.

Technically, MCF 3.2 adds AI predictive scaling with NVIDIA DGX and AWS Trainium for GenAI bursting— a Fortune 50 retailer trained 45% faster across Azure ML and AetherCloud. Egress costs dropped 40% via eBPF/Cilium observability. Aether Outpost for Edge supports 5G MEC on Dell hardware, targeting IDC's $50 billion TAM.

These efforts diversify growth, tapping $120 billion multi-cloud spend by 2026 at 35% CAGR. We're founding Multi-Cloud Foundation members with IBM/HashiCorp, pushing CNCF projects like Crossplane. Q3 guidance: $1.3 billion, 55% YoY growth, with 3.2x pipeline.

Now I'll turn the call over to Michael Chen to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we had a stellar financial performance in the Q2. Revenue grew by 32% year-over-year to $25.6 billion, significantly outpacing industry averages. Our gross margin was 78%, reflecting our pricing power and efficient cost management. Our operating margin was 35%.

Cloud services revenue remains the cornerstone, outperforming in this market. For the quarter ended June 30, 2024, it reached $25.6 billion, up 18% quarter-over-quarter from $21.7 billion in Q1, and 32% YoY from $19.4 billion in Q2 FY2023—our 15th straight quarter of accelerating growth, beating Gartner's 22% cloud market forecast.

Growth drivers: AI/ML workloads surged 152% YoY to $8.2 billion (32% of total), powered by AetherAI for 4,500+ enterprises on NVIDIA H100 and Aether Graviton4 Arm instances. Hyperscalers in healthcare/finance drove 85% compute utilization, up from 72%, like our U.S. bank deal echoing JPMorgan-AWS.

IaaS grew 28% YoY to $12.1 billion on elastic compute/storage; Aether Object Storage (S3-compatible) hit 45% YoY to $4.3 billion for data lakes, with 35-40% TCO savings vs. Azure/Google via zero-egress fees.

PaaS/SaaS rose 42% YoY to $5.3 billion; Aether Lambda exceeded 10 trillion invocations, up 60% QoQ, plus Aether Functions Edge for 1,200 net new DevOps logos.

Regionally: North America 52% ($13.3 billion, 29% YoY, $12M ACV for top 500). EMEA 48% YoY to $4.8 billion on GDPR sovereign clouds in Germany/France. APAC 62% to $4.1 billion via Mumbai/Jakarta, Indonesia $450M RPO. LatAm 11% to $1.2 billion.

We invested $2.1 billion capex in sustainable DCs (85% renewables). RPO $142 billion, up 39% YoY, 65% converting in 12 months.

Tailwinds: GenAI, edge for 5G IoT (Aether Edge Mesh 500 PB), EU Data Act. Risks: GPU supply, mitigated by NVIDIA/AMD contracts. Q3 cloud revenue guide: $27.2-27.8 billion, 20-22% QoQ.

Now, I'll hand it over to Dr. Vasquez for a technical update.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Michael. From a technology perspective, we made significant strides in several key areas this quarter. We are proud to announce the general availability of our new AetherAI platform, which offers unparalleled performance and scalability.

Energy efficiency and sustainability are central to our tech roadmap and financial positioning as the third-largest hyperscaler serving 45,000 customers with $18.7 billion TTM revenue. Gartner sees the market at $1.2 trillion by 2030; our efforts drive margins, compliance, retention.

Q2 PUE averaged 1.18 (down from 1.25 YoY, vs. industry 1.5), cutting energy costs 12% per rack, saving $245 million opex. Portfolio: 48 facilities, 12.5M sq ft, 8.5 TWh/year.

Pillars: operational efficiency, renewables, innovative infra.

Efficiency: Graviton4 across 65% compute (40% better TOPS efficiency, 25% less idle); AetherML TPUs v5e 2.8x lower power/token vs. H100. Direct-to-chip liquid cooling in 22 DCs cuts 45%, Virginia PUE to 1.09, +30% racks/MW. WUE 0.12 L/kWh (28% better) via adiabatic/zero-water pilots; Arizona 35% freshwater cut.

Renewables: 68% global energy (up from 52%), on track 100% by 2026. 4.2 GW PPAs with Ørsted/NextEra; Europe 95% via 1.8 GW Dutch wind (CBAM hedge). U.S. IRA credits $450M Nevada/Texas. APAC 80% Singapore/Tokyo (500 MWp solar, H2 pilots); China JV 55% nuclear.

Scope 1+2 emissions down 18% to 2.1M tCO2e despite 35% capacity growth. Scope 3: carbon-aware scheduling in AetherOptix cuts 14% for adopters.

Infra: $3.2B 2024 capex; Sweden Zero Carbon Campus (1 GW, geothermal, immersion cooling PUE<1.05, $15M heat revenue). Sustainable Reservations: 20% discounts, $1.2B ACV.

Accretive: +220bps EBITDA to 38.5%. 62% RFPs mandate SLAs; Cloud Sustainability Alliance work on Carbon Awareness API.

Risks: chip supply, regs like SB253. Targets: PUE 1.10 by 2026, net-zero 2030, $1B savings. AI energy (10% global by 2028) favors us.

I'll now pass it to Raj Patel for a product roadmap update.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Dr. Vasquez. This quarter, we launched Aether Shield Enterprise, a game-changing solution for regulated workloads in healthcare, finance, and government. Early customer feedback has been overwhelmingly positive. We are seeing strong demand and a rapid increase in adoption.

Our security and compliance leadership differentiates us, fueling 28% YoY growth in high-compliance verticals (42% of ARR, up from 35%). Gartner: 75% enterprises prioritize certified providers by 2025.

Q3 achievements: Third SOC 2 Type II (100% infra: Aether Compute, ObjectForge, Helix K8s; 250 controls, zero major findings; added AI accelerator).

PCI DSS 4.0 Level 1 (95% services; Stripe/Adyen partners; top-5 bank $18M ARR).

HITRUST CSF r2 Common 2 (85%; 400 controls; HIPAA workloads +35% to $450M ARR, Cleveland Clinic-like).

FedRAMP Moderate ATO (80% portfolio; DoD $120M data lakes).

EU: ISO 27001/17/34; CSA STAR Level 2 (98%). APAC: IRAP PROTECTED Sydney/Singapore; China MP-SC with Alibaba (12% APAC revenue).

92% infra certified, 99.7% pass rates, NPS 78 (vs. 62 avg).

Tech: Zero-trust/mTLS/Istio; Splunk+Nexara Sentinel AI (2.5M anomalies/day, MTTD<5min); PQC beta (Kyber/Dilithium). $45M invest, 40% less breach success.

Regions: NA 55% growth (FedRAMP/CISA); EMEA 25% QoQ (GDPR); APAC 42% (PDPA/My Number).

Engine: 35% shorter cycles, 22% Shield attach ($0.02/GB/mo, $65M upsell), 20% lower TCO vs. hyperscalers.

Ahead: FedRAMP High, C5 Type 2, AMD SEV-SNP 50%. $150B regulated TAM by 2027; 99.99% SLA to $2.5B ARR FY25.

Now, back to Sarah Kline.

Sarah Kline:
Thank you, Raj. We are incredibly excited about the future. We believe our investments in innovation, our commitment to customer success, and our talented team will continue to drive strong growth and value creation.

A key non-operational factor on results: FX fluctuations, with 55% revenue international. Q2 total $25.6B, +18% YoY reported, 24% constant currency. FX shaved $148M (5.2 pts).

EMEA 60% drag (euro -7.2%, GBP -4.8%; €1.2B bookings like Siemens hybrid; const curr 28% vs. 19% reported). APAC 25% (yen -9.1%, AUD -3.5%; AI 32% const vs. 21%). LATAM/other 15% (BRL/INR -5-6%).

Third straight quarter pressure ($420M FY23 headwind vs. FY22 tailwind); peers like AWS 4-6% drag. Consumption model exposes 65% to spot FX.

Mitigations: 70% hedged ($42M Q2 gain); localization (Tokyo/São Paulo/Dublin DCs, 15% APAC/LATAM neutral); dynamic pricing in 28 currencies.

Ex-FX: NRR 118%, RPO +22% to $142B, AI +45%. Q3 FX 3-5% headwind ($100-120M); guide $27.2-27.8B, 20-22% const curr growth.

With that, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, to ask a question, press star then one. Our first question comes from Johnathan Hale with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Johnathan Hale:
Thanks for taking my question, and congrats on a strong quarter. Sarah, could you expand on the AI workload acceleration and how it's influencing customer migrations?

Sarah Kline:
Thanks, Johnathan. Absolutely, AI is a standout, with workloads up 152% YoY to $8.2 billion. Customers like major banks are ramping AetherAI for LLMs on H100s and Graviton4, hitting 85% utilization. This drives IaaS/PaaS growth as enterprises consolidate data lakes and go serverless, with TCO savings of 35-40%. We're seeing durable demand via $142B RPO.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong:
Great, thanks. Michael, on the FX headwinds and margins—how are you thinking about hedging into FY25, and any pricing adjustments?

Michael Chen:
Hi Lisa, thanks. FX was a 5.2 point drag this quarter, but our 70% hedge program and localization like new edge DCs limit net impact. Margins held strong at 78% gross/35% op thanks to efficiencies. No aggressive repricing; we're guiding const curr growth 20-22% Q3, with NRR 118% underscoring demand.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Ruiz with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Ruiz:
Thanks, team. Elena, impressive PUE progress—how does sustainability tie into your tech roadmap for edge and AI, and competitive moat?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
David, great question. PUE 1.18 drives $245M savings, with Graviton4/liquid cooling enabling denser AI. Renewables at 68% support edge like Aether Edge Mesh for 5G IoT. This builds moat—62% RFPs demand SLAs—targeting 1.10 PUE by 2026 amid AI's energy surge.

Sarah Kline:
Thank you for your insightful questions and your continued interest in AetherCloud Technologies. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
